## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing respawn and render into a single particle pass while letting the compiler auto-vectorize integration can approach the streaming ceiling by halving memory traffic.

## Layout & approach
The AoS layout at 69 B/p offers 28 hot bytes (41%) for loop 1 (age+pos+vel) and 32 hot bytes (47%) for loop 2 (color+pos+seed), meaning 59% and 53% of each cache-line fill is dead weight dragged through the line filler. The mask intermediate adds 1 B/particle. The fused loop 2 should read each particle once for both respawn-decide and render, halving struct traffic versus two passes. Loop 1's auto-vectorization operates component-wise within a single particle — `vmulps`/`vaddps` on 4 floats — not across particles, at one particle per iteration and stride 68B. The working set spills L1d at N≈474 and L2 at N≈7598, but with only 41–47% hot bytes the effective traffic is roughly halved, which should cushion the spills if the codegen can stream.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p-vs-N curve is remarkably flat: at q=0.01 it ranges from 21.99 (N=320, L1d) to 25.04 (N=10M, DRAM) — a 14% rise across four cache regimes. The L1d→L2 spill at N≈474 is invisible (22.0→22.3 ns/p). The L2→L3 transition at N≈7598 shows a slight bump to 24.3 ns/p that recedes at N=10000 (23.7 ns/p). The L3→DRAM transition at N≈243148 produces a gentle rise from ~23 to ~25 ns/p. This flatness is not prefetch friendliness — it is the signature of a frontend-bound algo that barely notices the memory hierarchy. The dense grid resolves no knee because there is none to resolve.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.0–3.1 GB/s — only 16–24% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling, and 4–6× above the 5.437 ns/p memory floor. The algo is decisively frontend-bound, not bandwidth-bound: backend_stall is 0.0% across all profiles while frontend_stall consumes 64–72%. The low achieved GB/s is a symptom of stalled execution, not saturated memory. Against the naive scalar baseline the algo is 0.92–1.01× — essentially identical — confirming the auto-vec and fusion provide no net benefit. Against the winner it is 1.8–3.4× slower: 2.97× at q=0.01/N=320, 2.39× at N=10M, collapsing to 1.84× at q=0.5/N=320. Death rate is the equalizer: at q=0.5 the branchy respawn path dominates and the algo converges to 0.99–1.01× baseline.

## Assembly
Loop 1 achieves partial within-particle vectorization: `vmovups` loads 16B of pos, `vmovsd` loads 8B of vel, `vshufps`/`vinsertps` rearranges components, then `vmulps`/`vaddps` operate on 4 floats — but one particle per iteration at stride 0x44 (68B). This is component-wise vec, not lane-wise, so it cannot amortize the 59% dead bytes per line fill. Loop 2 is the catastrophe: 351 insns/iter with 35 conditional branches, select-based via 12 `cmovae` chains and 31 byte-granular scatter stores (`movzx`, `add`, `cmp`, `cmovae`, `mov BYTE PTR` — repeated per RGBA channel). The `vucomiss` chains for color clamping and the `call` to spawn on death inflate the instruction footprint beyond the µop cache, explaining the 64–72% frontend stall. The byte-granular framebuffer writes cannot coalesce into cache-line stores, capping achieved bandwidth at 24% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo is 0.92–1.01× of naive (no improvement) and 1.8–3.4× slower than the winner at every measured point. The component-wise auto-vectorization in loop 1 cannot overcome the 59% dead-byte fraction in the AoS layout, and the fused loop 2's 351-insn/iter body with 35 branches and 31 byte-granular scatters creates a 64–72% frontend stall that no cache regime or death rate can rescue. At q=0.5 the algo converges to exactly 1.0× baseline (0.99–1.01×), proving the fusion provides zero net benefit once respawn dominates.
